summary: Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University in 2015 and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo in 2017.
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Di Cosmo is a historian of Sinology and Central Asia. After completing his PhD at Indiana University, he held posts at Cambridge, Harvard, and Columbia, and became Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study around 2003.

Nicolaas Johannes Krom (1883–1945) was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and was a professor at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.
Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam and Moscow State University. He held an academic post at Leiden University beginning in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Silpakorn University and completed his doctorate under Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling. He held a post at Thammasat University attested in 2016–2017.

Nicolas Tournadre is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He has held positions at INALCO, Paris 8 University, and Aix-Marseille University, where he became a professor around 2011.
Nicole Baden is an expert in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Richard Baker as her traditional teacher and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO from around 1966 to 1977.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was a Danish scholar of Indology, Iranian studies, and linguistics. After studying in Copenhagen, Bonn under Christian Lassen, and Oxford, he served as professor and Rektor at the University of Copenhagen.
Nigel Allan worked in history and archaeology, serving as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust in 1993, succeeding Marianne Winder.

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) was an Indian scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden, later serving as Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts at Calcutta University (1946–1965) and Director of IIAS (1965–1970).

Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her master's degree at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes, having also studied under Géza Bethlenfalvy.

Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin (1777–1853) was a scholar of Sinology and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Kazan Theological Academy, he held an appointment at the Département asiatique around 1826.

Niklas Luhmann (1927–1998) was a German philosopher and sociologist. He studied at the University of Freiburg and Harvard University, and served as a professor at Bielefeld University from around 1968 to 1993.

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and held a position at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2013.

Nina Mirnig is an Indologist who completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2010. She has held research posts at the University of Groningen and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a British philosopher of religion educated at Oxford. He was Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (1967–1982) and J. F. Rowny Professor at UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who earned his doctorate from Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop in 2015. He served at the Nepal Research Centre and later held research positions at Naples and Leiden.
